response.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT 
    o.ordertune,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) as cnt
  FROM orders o
  INNER JOIN riskandmargin rm ON o.recordvault = rm.ordervault
  GROUP BY o.ordertune
),
avg_overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) as avg_cnt
  FROM counts
)
SELECT 
  AVG(c.cnt) as average_count,
  AVG(c.cnt - ao.avg_cnt) as average_excess
FROM counts c
CROSS JOIN avg_overall ao
WHERE c.cnt > ao.avg_cnt;

assumptions.assumption: The schema allows multiple risk/margin records per order. Counting 'risk/margin-matched orders' means counting distinct orders (by orderspivot), not the total number of matches. An order with 3 risk/margin records is one matched order, not three.

alternatives.interpretation: Count total matches instead of distinct orders—if an order has multiple risk/margin records, count each match separately.
alternatives.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT 
    o.ordertune,
    COUNT(*) as cnt
  FROM orders o
  INNER JOIN riskandmargin rm ON o.recordvault = rm.ordervault
  GROUP BY o.ordertune
),
avg_overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) as avg_cnt
  FROM counts
)
SELECT 
  AVG(c.cnt) as average_count,
  AVG(c.cnt - ao.avg_cnt) as average_excess
FROM counts c
CROSS JOIN avg_overall ao
WHERE c.cnt > ao.avg_cnt;
